description: Cointegration Pairs Trading. Structural/statistical-arbitrage mechanism: test whether pairs of related assets (BTC/ETH, Gold/gold-miner-equity) have a long-run stable price relationship (cointegration), which a mean-reverting spread trade can exploit without predicting either asset's absolute direction. Distinct from Direction A/B's directional prediction and Direction D's funding-rate carry -- this is a third, separate mechanism (statistical arbitrage on the SPREAD between two assets, not either asset's own price).
stopping_rule_doc: Stop testing a given pair if the Engle-Granger cointegration test fails (p >= 0.05) on the full available history -- no cointegration relationship means no valid basis for a pairs trade, regardless of how the spread looks visually.
sacred_holdout_path: N/A at the cointegration-existence-test stage (this is a structural/statistical test on the full historical relationship, not a fitted predictive model). A holdout would apply to a later stage (spread-trading strategy backtest), not this existence check.

Pre-registered BEFORE running the cointegration test, per the pre-registration discipline established this session (F27's lesson).

Stage 1 (this registry): does a cointegration relationship exist at all? Stage 2 (future, separate registration): if yes, backtest an actual spread-trading strategy with proper DK-test/label-shuffle/cost modeling -- do NOT skip straight from 'cointegrated' to 'tradeable' without that second stage.

hypotheses.name: BTC/ETH Cointegration Existence Test
hypotheses.methodology_note: A naive manual Engle-Granger (ADF on the OLS residual using STANDARD adfuller critical values) gave p=0.0441, which would have been misread as 'cointegrated' at the 0.05 threshold. This is a known trap: standard ADF critical values are wrong for a residual series whose generating regression was itself estimated (the cointegrating vector) -- the correct critical values (MacKinnon, used internally by statsmodels.tsa.stattools.coint()) are more stringent. Used the properly-adjusted test (p=0.1328) as the frozen, pre-registered verdict, not the naive one. REJECTED -- no valid statistical basis for a BTC/ETH pairs trade found.
hypotheses.hypothesis: log(BTCUSD) and log(ETHUSD) are cointegrated -- i.e. a linear combination of the two is stationary (mean-reverting), even though each individually is a non-stationary random walk. If true, the spread between them (properly hedge-ratio-weighted) can be traded as a mean-reversion strategy without taking a view on whether crypto broadly goes up or down.
hypotheses.economic_rationale: BTC and ETH are both large-cap crypto assets sharing overlapping investor base, correlated risk-on/risk-off flows, and (historically) high pairwise correlation -- a common a priori reason to expect a cointegrating relationship, though correlation alone does not imply cointegration.
data_dependencies: data/ETHUSD_D1.csv (already in repo, real historical data)
hypotheses.validation_plan: Engle-Granger test on full overlapping history -> if p<0.05, proceed to Stage 2 (spread-trading strategy backtest, separately registered). If p>=0.05, REJECT and do not proceed to Stage 2.

hypotheses.name: Gold Spot / Gold-Miner-Equity Cointegration Existence Test
hypotheses.methodology_note: GDX fetched live via yfinance (data/GDX_D1_yfinance.csv, 5076 rows, 2006-2026) since no local data existed. p=0.5455 -- not close to the 0.05 threshold, unlike BTC/ETH's borderline-but-still-failing 0.13. The a priori economic rationale (miners' revenue tied to spot) does NOT translate into a statistically detectable stationary spread over this 20-year window -- plausibly because miners carry substantial idiosyncratic risk (operating costs, hedging policy, jurisdiction/political risk, equity-market beta) that swamps the shared gold-price component over the long run, consistent with well-documented miner-vs-spot performance divergence in the literature.
hypotheses.instrument: XAUUSD vs. GDX (VanEck Gold Miners ETF)
hypotheses.hypothesis: Gold spot price and gold-miner-equity (GDX) are cointegrated -- miners' revenue is directly tied to the gold price, so a long-run equilibrium relationship is economically expected, with GDX carrying additional operating-leverage and equity-market beta that can temporarily de-couple it from spot before reverting.
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Gold miners are a leveraged play on gold price (fixed costs, variable revenue tied to spot) -- textbook cointegration candidate distinct from a funding-rate or momentum mechanism.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Engle-Granger test on full overlapping history -> if p<0.05, proceed to Stage 2. REJECTED, no Stage 2.
